metadata.title: 19वीं सदी में जीता एक भारत |“An India Living in the 19th Century”
metadata.description:
Part 2 of our ground report from the Satpura range in Nandurbar district reveals how mobile network dark zones continue to shape—and shatter—the lives of Adivasi communities.

With no connectivity, many tribal families are unable to access subsidised rations on time, pushing already vulnerable households deeper into distress.

The report also highlights a bridge project that began 13 years ago but remains incomplete, symbolising chronic neglect and broken promises by the system.

Beyond infrastructure failures, a far more silent crisis is unfolding—sickle cell anaemia, which is steadily claiming lives in tribal areas with little attention or support.

Yet, even amid neglect and suffering, there are small islands of hope—stories of resilience and courage that refuse to be erased.

This is an important ground report from one of India’s most marginalised regions, brought to you by Main Bhi Bharat, reported and edited by Shyam Sunder.
